notes: The colophon gives the era only as 'samvat'. The place, 'gaṃḍahādeśa' near the Gaṅgā, is probably the Gaṇḍaka (Gandak) country in North Bihar, and there a plain 'samvat' would normally be Vikrama Saṃvat. That makes VS 1674 more likely than the catalogue's queried ŚS. VS 1674 Māgha śukla 1 falls around 27–28 January 1618 CE. A rough mean-new-moon calculation puts pratipad at Saturday/Sunday, so the Sunday is plausible but not checked exactly. If the year were ŚS 1674, the date would fall in January 1753 CE. The words 'miśragosvādedāṃsaprasādāt' are marked corrupt with daggers by the cataloguer. A likely reading is 'miśragosvāmidevadāsaprasādāt', 'by the grace of Miśra Gosvāmin Devadāsa'. The person may be a teacher or patron of the scribe, but the colophon does not say which.
